articles.title: Flat vs segmented memory -- it's recursive
articles.summary: Rambles around computer science Diverting trains of thought, wasting precious time Flat vs segmented memory -- it's recursive My recent forays in x86 segmentation have made me notice a trend in the evolution of x86: the decline of fine-grained memory protection, both across the move to 64-bit and indeed before that in the fast system calling features. The explanation is possibly Unix: the dominance of Unix and its preference for flat address spaces, rather than segmented ones, arguably inherited from the PDP-11 or indeed PDP-7, meant that nobody wanted a 64-bit version of the segmentation features. WebAssembly is like a return to the programming model of OS/2 or some other non-Unix OSes, where flatness did not reign so supreme, and such non-flatness is still highly relevant to safety and security of course.

articles.title: The efficient frontier of LLM inference
articles.summary: Inference techniques either move a deployment along the latency-throughput frontier or push the entire frontier out, creating more efficiency to allocate. Authors Philip Kiely have developed the GLM-5.3 model, which offers a fraction of the cost of other LLMs while maintaining high performance. The efficient frontier of LLM inference shows the range of optimal combinations when trading off between latency and throughput, and techniques such as batch sizing and quantization can be used to target specific points on the frontier. By understanding and managing tradeoffs, inference engineers can optimize their models for specific use cases and applications.

articles.summary: The RangeFrom iterator is not designed to yield values beyond the largest value in the range, which can lead to unexpected behavior when overflow-checks are turned off. This is because the internal counter is incremented before the value is yielded, causing the iterator to overflow before the final value is reached. This can result in the iterator producing incorrect results, such as printing a value before it is actually yielded.

As a CNA, the project can now issue its own CVEs without involving an outsider, but it still assesses and grades the severity of issues based on its own criteria.
